findings.message: Independently re-checked brief.json's word-set concept fields against src/literacy/taxonomy.ts's detectors by hand (not just trusting the automated report). r-controlled-words (dark, door, storm, corner, turn, further, carve, torch) all contain ar/er/ir/or/ur, matching the r-controlled detector; ck-words (rock, lock, trick, clock, knock, crack, stack, pocket) all contain a vowel + ck, matching the digraph-ck detector. No concept/word mismatch in this job's brief (unlike the defect found and fixed in two sibling jobs this run).

Spot-checked the analyzer's raw counts against the draft text by grep: exact-token counts for "turn" (4: loose-panel, old-logbook, into-the-walls, ending-rush-alone) and "door" (8: ask-around/three-knocks, pells-shed, gathering x2, into-the-walls, theo-marsh, ending-jump-to-ghost, ending-rush-alone) match reports/literacy.r1.json's perWord figures exactly, so I trust the rest of its per-word and per-route numbers rather than re-deriving all 16 words by hand.

Both word sets clear their minOccurrences (r-controlled 40/10, ck-words 56/12), every declared word appears at least twice, and every word is used naturally in varied senses (e.g. "crack" as a crack of space, a crack in the wall, and the sound of a panel opening; "stack" of chairs/cushions/tiles; "lock"/"key"/"trick" woven into the mystery's own vocabulary, not listed off). No forced rhymes or word-dump sentences.

Traced the passage graph by hand: reaching any ending other than ending-rush-alone requires passing through both the closet-search→loose-panel→find-brass-key branch (brass key) and the ask-around→pells-shed→old-logbook branch (logbook-page clue) before gathering→threshold→into-the-walls→theo-marsh, so both word sets genuinely appear on every route to every ending, not just on one branch; this matches the word-sets-on-every-route and perEndingRoute figures in the report.

"door" is grouped under r-controlled via the spelling-pattern detector's substring match on "or", and it is pronounced with the same r-coloured vowel as "for"/"storm"/"torch", so it is a legitimate (if orthographically oor-spelled) r-controlled word, not a mismatch. A tutor whose program treats "oor" words as their own sub-pattern separate from ar/er/ir/or/ur may want to flag that distinction when mapping this story's word set to their own scope and sequence.

maxSentenceWords (18) is respected throughout; the longest sentences found by hand-count (e.g. in loose-panel, ask-around, into-the-walls, theo-marsh, ending-honest-ask) land at exactly 18 words, none over. Continuity constraints are honoured: no ghost, curse or other supernatural being is ever confirmed real; Theo Marsh winding Augusta Cragmoor's old clock is the human explanation; no violence, real brands or romance appear.

Skills practised: this story practises decoding r-controlled vowel words and ck-digraph words in natural mystery-solving context, holding and reusing a small set of recurring words (dark, door, further, lock, knock, crack, pocket, and others) across every branch so the patterns are met repeatedly rather than once. It also exercises sequencing (tracking a three-knock, one-knock pattern and a wind-rest-knock routine across several pages before the payoff matches), inference (reading Theo's tiredness, Mr. Pell's familiarity with the clock, and Augusta's journal entry to infer the real explanation before it is stated outright), vocabulary from context via the glossary (workshop, founder, corridor, headmaster and others, each defined where it first appears), and comprehension through choices that let the reader compare evidence (key vs. clue) before deciding how to approach Theo, with the four non-rush endings differing by how trusting or hasty that approach was.

shelfSummary.blurb: Rowan and Dessa trace a nightly knock through the walls of a foggy boarding school, finding a hidden workshop and a kept secret instead of a ghost. The story practises r-controlled vowel words and ck-digraph words throughout, alongside sequencing clues and inferring a character's motives before judging him.

findings.message: The 'gathering' passage (Comparing Notes) is the only connector between the closet-search branch (which yields the brass-key item in find-brass-key) and the ask-around branch (which yields the logbook-page clue in old-logbook). Every exit from either branch routes back to 'gathering' and there is no edge from one branch straight into the other (confirmed in reports/graph.r1.json edges). The locked choice at threshold ('open-hatch-calm') requires both brass-key and logbook-page, which can only be collected by visiting both branches, which forces the reader to pass back through the identical, unchanged 'gathering' text at least twice (e.g. start -> closet-search -> loose-panel -> find-brass-key -> gathering [1st read] -> ask-around -> pells-shed -> old-logbook -> gathering [2nd read, same text] -> threshold). This is exactly the kind of forced re-read of already-seen pages, to collect an item/clue and reach the four 'good' endings reachable only via the locked choice (ending-trust, ending-honest-ask, ending-call-pell, ending-jump-to-ghost all sit behind into-the-walls/theo-marsh, which is only reachable through open-hatch-calm or by abandoning the key/clue path for ending-rush-alone). The 'gathering' passage text and choice set (gather-to-closet / gather-to-ask / gather-to-threshold) never change to reflect what the reader has already collected, so the second visit is a verbatim repeat. Recommend either letting a branch route directly into the other without returning through an unchanged hub, or varying the hub text/choices once an item/clue is already held, or dropping the two-item lock requirement so a single branch suffices.

Location naming is inconsistent between the start/closet-search passages, which always call this room the 'storage closet' (start choice 'to-closet': 'Search the storage closet at the end of the hall'; closet-search title 'Into the Storage Closet'), and the locked-choice hint at threshold, which calls it the 'storage room' ('You need the brass key from the storage room and the logbook page from the office.'). A reader using the hint to retrace which passage to revisit may be confused by the mismatched name.

loose-panel foreshadows that the hidden lock 'needed a key, not a trick, and the answer must lie further in these walls,' but the two choices offered are 'Pry the panel open anyway' (which succeeds immediately, by force, with no key) or go back. The panel is never actually unlocked with a key -- it is pried open despite the text's claim that a key (not force) was required, and the brass key found inside is instead used later on a different lock (the threshold hatch). This is a minor puzzle-logic inconsistency that could confuse an attentive young reader tracking cause and effect.

Diffed story.r1.json against story.r2.json by hand (structural JSON diff, not just the revision notes) to see the whole edit surface. The only changes are: loose-panel's two choice labels and its foreshadowing paragraph; new setFlags (have-brass-key, have-logbook-page) on find-brass-key and old-logbook; gathering's three choices gaining requires/lockedHint and its two narration paragraphs being reworded; threshold's open-hatch-calm lockedHint swapping "storage room" for "storage closet"; and the version bump. Nothing else moved, so my re-check below covers the full change set the brief described.

Re-checked brief.json's word-set concept fields against src/literacy/taxonomy.ts's detectors again on this revision (word lists are unchanged from r1): r-controlled-words (dark, door, storm, corner, turn, further, carve, torch) all contain ar/er/ir/or/ur; ck-words (rock, lock, trick, clock, knock, crack, stack, pocket) all contain a vowel + ck. Still no concept/word mismatch, confirmed again rather than carried over blindly from the r1 review.

Confirmed 'storage room' is gone from the draft entirely (grep for both terms finds only 'storage closet', in start's to-closet choice, closet-search's own text, gathering's reworded narration and its gather-to-closet lockedHint, and threshold's open-hatch-calm lockedHint). The naming inconsistency QA flagged on r1 is fixed everywhere, not just at the one site QA pointed to.

Loose-panel's rewritten foreshadowing ('It looked too small for any real key.' / 'Maybe a good, sharp trick would crack it open. The real answer still lay further inside, past this one small door.') now matches the actual by-force resolution at find-brass-key ('Rowan pried at the panel until it opened with a soft crack'); no key is used on that lock anywhere in the story. The two reworded choice labels ('Try a trick and pry the panel open' / 'Leave the lock alone; go back and tell Dessa first') agree with this and no longer assert the dropped 'needs a key' claim. Continuity holds: no ghost, curse or other supernatural being is confirmed real anywhere in r2, and Theo Marsh winding Augusta Cragmoor's old clock remains the sole, human resolution at theo-marsh and in all five endings.

maxSentenceWords (18) is respected in every new or reworded sentence: both loose-panel foreshadowing sentences (15, 8, 9, 12 words), both reworded gathering narration sentences (13, 11, 13, 17 words), and both new lockedHints (10 and 12 words) and the edited threshold lockedHint (16 words) all land under 18 by hand count. The rest of the story is untouched text already verified against the 18-word limit on r1. The analyzer's own sentence-length check uses a looser 20-word threshold and should not be read as confirming the brief's actual 18-word limit; hand-counting the changed text was necessary and it clears both thresholds.

Traced the passage graph by hand with the new flag gates at gathering. have-brass-key is set only by find-brass-key (reached only via closet-search -> loose-panel -> pry-panel); have-logbook-page is set only by old-logbook (reached only via ask-around -> pells-shed -> see-records). On a reader's first visit to gathering neither flag is set, so both branch choices are open; once a branch is completed, gathering's matching choice locks with its lockedHint and cannot be re-entered, while the other branch and gather-to-threshold stay open. Reaching threshold with both brass-key and logbook-page (required for every ending except ending-rush-alone) still forces passing through both branches exactly once each, so the word sets' presence on every route is structurally unchanged from r1; the forced identical-content repeat visit QA flagged is now mechanically impossible, confirmed by reading the choice graph, not just by trusting the revision notes.

Re-verified the word-set numbers against reports/literacy.r2.json rather than trusting the revision notes' self-reported figures: r-controlled-words 41/10 (up from 40 on r1), ck-words 59/12 (up from 56), no missing words, and perEndingRoute is identical across all 5 endings to r1's figures (e.g. ending-trust 14 r-controlled/26 ck, ending-rush-alone 15 r-controlled/14 ck), consistent with the edited passages (loose-panel, gathering) sitting off the shortest route to any ending. Both sets still clear their minimums on every route with margin.

The new lockedHint text itself ('You already found the brass key in the storage closet.' / 'You already learned the clue from Mr. Pell and the old logbook.') uses none of the two target word sets' words, unlike the threshold lockedHint it was modelled on, which also has none. This is informational only, not a defect: hint text is short, functional UI copy rather than narrative prose, and the story clears its minimums comfortably without it.

On a reader's third visit to gathering (after both branches are done), the narration still says 'Let's see what else we can learn before we go further,' even though the only thing left to do is go to threshold; the locked choices and their lockedHints make this unambiguous mechanically, but a narrative pass that varied gathering's own line on that specific visit (e.g. once both flags are set) would read a little more naturally. This is a narrative polish note, not a literacy defect, and not blocking: comprehension and word-set properties are unaffected and the scene remains clear.

findings.message: The r1 major finding about a forced duplicate read of the unchanged 'gathering' hub passage is not actually fixed. The fix adds requires.notFlags + lockedHint to gathering's 'gather-to-closet' and 'gather-to-ask' choices (gated on have-brass-key / have-logbook-page), which only stops the reader from re-entering an already-completed branch a second time -- that was never the problem described in review-2-qa.r1.json. The exact repro route quoted in that review is untouched and still the only way (besides the single-item-only ending-rush-alone path) to collect both brass-key and logbook-page for the dual-locked 'open-hatch-calm' choice at threshold and reach the four best endings: start -> to-closet -> closet-search -> pry-board -> loose-panel -> pry-panel -> find-brass-key (sets have-brass-key) -> key-to-dessa -> gathering [1st visit, reads the same 4 paragraphs] -> gather-to-ask -> ask-around -> find-pell -> pells-shed -> see-records -> old-logbook (sets have-logbook-page) -> logbook-to-dessa -> gathering [2nd visit, byte-for-byte identical paragraphs and the same gather-to-threshold/gather-to-closet/gather-to-ask choice set, confirmed by direct read of drafts/story.r2.json lines 228-254] -> gather-to-threshold -> threshold. Because gathering's paragraphs never vary by flag state (confirmed src/engine/story-engine.ts choicesFor/Reader.tsx render every choice, including locked ones with a disabled button and lockedHint, so the two visits render identically except one locked-choice hint), the reader still reads this passage's full text twice, verbatim, as a mandatory step to reach the dual-item lock and the 4 triumph/bittersweet endings gated behind it. This remains a major finding per the review criteria ('a route that makes the reader go back over pages already read ... to reach an ending'). Recommend one of the original suggestions that actually touches the hub content: let one branch feed into the other directly without an intermediate return to gathering, vary gathering's own paragraphs once a flag is already set (not just the branch choices), or drop the two-item requirement at threshold so a single branch suffices.

Diffed story.r2.json against story.r3.json by hand. The only structural change is the QA-driven restructuring: two new one-time transition passages, closet-report and clue-report, now receive the return choices that used to flow straight back into gathering from the closet-search branch (back-to-dessa-1, no-key-no-trick, key-to-dessa, tell-dessa-light, to-gathering-a-end, to-gathering-a-end2) and the ask-around branch (skip-to-gathering-b, thanks-back, logbook-to-dessa, enough-reading-to-gathering, to-gathering-b-end, to-gathering-b-end2). Each new passage has exactly two gated choices: one to gathering (open only while the other branch's flag is not yet set) and one straight to threshold (open only once it is). gathering's own narration, its three choices, threshold, both branches' existing passages, and both endings-side content are byte-for-byte unchanged from r2. Version bumped to 3.

Traced the full graph by hand in both branch orders to confirm the QA fix actually works. Closet-first order: start -> closet-search -> loose-panel -> find-brass-key (sets have-brass-key) -> closet-report -> gathering (first and only visit; closet-report-to-wall is locked here because have-logbook-page isn't set yet) -> ask-around -> pells-shed -> old-logbook (sets have-logbook-page) -> clue-report -> threshold (clue-report-to-gathering is now locked because have-brass-key is set, so clue-report-to-wall is the only option) -> into-the-walls -> theo-marsh -> ending. Clue-first order is the mirror image and also passes through gathering exactly once before reaching threshold. In both orders the reader reaches the four best endings (ending-trust, ending-honest-ask, ending-call-pell, ending-jump-to-ghost) having read gathering's unchanged narration exactly once, never twice verbatim. The short no-item route to the fifth ending (ending-rush-alone), e.g. start -> closet-search -> closet-report -> gathering -> threshold -> climb-vent-alone, also only visits gathering once, since neither flag is set and both closet-report-to-wall and clue-report-to-wall stay locked until the matching flag is set. The QA-flagged forced double verbatim read is mechanically eliminated in every route I traced, not just on the two routes the designer's report checked.

closet-report and clue-report are reasonable one-time connective beats (Rowan returning to Dessa, a believable in-fiction reason to pause before the next branch), not degenerate 'you got an item, pick a destination' text, and they respect maxSentenceWords (18): closet-report's three sentences hand-count at 14, 13 and 11 words; clue-report's at 14, 14 and 11 words. However their closing line is verbatim identical in both passages: "There was still more to learn before nine o'clock came again." Combined with how similar the rest of each passage is ("Dessa was waiting by the common room door, ready/eager to hear..."), a reader who takes one branch then the other will read two near-identical paragraphs back to back in the clue-first or closet-first full exploration order, which is milder than the QA-flagged bug but still a bit formulaic. Not a comprehension or word-set defect and not blocking, but worth a narrative pass to vary the closing line between the two passages (e.g. tie it to which clue is still missing) so the fix doesn't trade one repetition for a smaller one.

Checked closet-report and clue-report against the brief's continuity constraints. Neither passage confirms a ghost or any supernatural being; both stay strictly in the register of 'Rowan went to tell Dessa something.' Both read correctly regardless of which upstream passage the reader arrived from (closet-report is reachable from five different closet-branch exits, clue-report from five different ask-around-branch exits) because neither passage references specific items, clues or discoveries by name, so there is no risk of a passage claiming knowledge the reader doesn't yet have, or contradicting what happened on a shorter sub-path. No continuity violation found. Theo Marsh winding Augusta Cragmoor's clock remains the sole human resolution at theo-marsh and in all five endings, unchanged from r2.

Verified the restructuring's effect on word-set coverage against reports/literacy.r3.json rather than trusting the revision notes: r-controlled-words totalOccurrences is 44/10 (matches the designer's claimed rise from 41) and ck-words is 61/12 (matches the claimed rise from 59), both with missingWords: [] and meetsMinimum: true. perEndingRoute lists all five endings well above both minimums (r-controlled 12-13 per route, ck 14-26 per route). I hand-counted both word sets on two short routes to ending-rush-alone myself (closet-first: start/closet-search/closet-report/gathering/threshold/ending-rush-alone, and clue-first: start/ask-around/clue-report/gathering/threshold/ending-rush-alone) and got r-controlled totals in the 12-15 range and ck totals around 13, which lands close to the report's reported 13/14 for that ending (exact ties in 'shortest route' depend on BFS tie-breaking, so small differences from my manual count are expected) and confirms the figures are real, not stale or inflated. I also confirmed every word in both sets (dark, door, storm, corner, turn, further, carve, torch; rock, lock, trick, clock, knock, crack, stack, pocket) is still used naturally in the surviving, unchanged branch passages and in the two new transition passages contribute no new target-word occurrences themselves (closet-report and clue-report contain none of the eight target words in either set, by design, since they're short connective beats), which is consistent with the designer's totals being driven by the unchanged branch content, not by new text in the restructuring.

Re-checked brief.json's word-set concept fields against src/literacy/taxonomy.ts's detectors once more despite no expected change: r-controlled-words (dark, door, storm, corner, turn, further, carve, torch) each contain ar/er/ir/or/ur, matching concept r-controlled's detector /(ar|er|ir|or|ur)/; ck-words (rock, lock, trick, clock, knock, crack, stack, pocket) each contain a vowel + ck, matching concept digraph-ck's detector /[aeiou]ck/. Word lists and detectors are unchanged from r1/r2, confirmed fresh rather than carried over.

Skills practised: this story practises decoding r-controlled vowel words and ck-digraph words in natural mystery-solving context, holding and reusing a small set of recurring words (dark, door, further, lock, knock, crack, pocket, and others) across every branch and both read orders so the patterns are met repeatedly rather than once. It also exercises sequencing (tracking a three-knock, one-knock pattern and a wind-rest-knock routine across several pages before the payoff matches), inference (reading Theo's tiredness, Mr. Pell's familiarity with the clock, and Augusta's journal entry to infer the real explanation before it is stated outright), vocabulary from context via the glossary (workshop, founder, corridor, headmaster and others, each defined where it first appears), and comprehension through choices that let the reader compare evidence (key vs. clue) before deciding how to approach Theo, with the four non-rush endings differing by how trusting or hasty that approach was. The two new transition passages (closet-report, clue-report) add brief sequencing and engagement beats but don't change the skill set the story as a whole practises.

findings.message: The r3 self-report's central claim ('gathering is visited at most once on any route to any ending') is false. It only holds for the two routes the narrative-designer actually traced (finish closet branch completely, then finish ask-around branch completely, or vice versa). It does not hold if the reader uses either branch's own designed 'bail out early' choices before finishing it. Repro, reachable through the real engine with no out-of-range choices (checked choice-by-choice against drafts/story.r3.json and against src/engine/story-engine.ts's meetsCondition/applyEffects semantics -- flags/items/clues only ever accumulate, never clear, and choice availability has no memory of prior visits): start -[to-closet]-> closet-search -[back-to-dessa-1]-> closet-report (flags={}, so closet-report-to-gathering's requires.notFlags:[have-logbook-page] is satisfied) -[closet-report-to-gathering]-> gathering (VISIT #1, reads 'Comparing Notes' in full) -[gather-to-closet, unlocked because have-brass-key is still not set]-> closet-search (VISIT #2 of this exact passage, verbatim) -[pry-board]-> loose-panel -[pry-panel]-> find-brass-key (sets have-brass-key, adds brass-key) -[key-to-dessa]-> closet-report (VISIT #2 of this exact passage, verbatim; closet-report-to-gathering is still unlocked because have-logbook-page is still not set, regardless of have-brass-key) -[closet-report-to-gathering]-> gathering (VISIT #2, reads the identical 4 paragraphs again) -[gather-to-ask, unlocked because have-logbook-page is still not set]-> ask-around -[find-pell]-> pells-shed -[see-records]-> old-logbook (sets have-logbook-page, adds clue) -[logbook-to-dessa]-> clue-report (clue-report-to-wall is now unlocked because have-brass-key is set) -[clue-report-to-wall]-> threshold -[open-hatch-calm, both items held]-> into-the-walls -[step-quiet]-> theo-marsh -[show-understanding]-> ending-trust. On this single, legal route to one of the four best (triumph/bittersweet) endings, 'gathering' is read twice verbatim, and 'closet-search' and 'closet-report' are each also read twice verbatim -- i.e. the reader goes back over pages already read in order to collect the brass-key item and ultimately reach the ending. This is the same defect reported in review-2-qa.r1 (major) and review-4-qa.r2 (major), now reachable via the branches' own pre-existing bail choices ('back-to-dessa-1' at closet-search, 'no-key-no-trick' at loose-panel; symmetric bail choices 'skip-to-gathering-b' at ask-around and 'thanks-back' at pells-shed produce the mirror-image route with clue-report/ask-around duplicated instead). closet-report-to-gathering's and clue-report-to-gathering's requires only check the OTHER branch's flag (have-logbook-page / have-brass-key respectively), never whether gathering itself, or the branch just exited, has already been visited, so bailing out of a branch before collecting its item and finishing that branch on a later pass re-triggers the whole hub loop and re-reads the branch's own passages. Neither reports/graph.r3.json nor npm run validate:stories catches this because the graph validator only checks reachability/soft-locks/single-choice structurally, not whether a route re-reads passage text already seen -- confirmed by reading src/validation/graph.ts in full. Recommend tracking a 'visited-gathering' style flag (or one flag per branch-attempted, not per-item-collected) so a bailed branch cannot reopen the hub loop after the reader already passed through gathering once, or restructure so closet-report/clue-report route on 'has the OTHER branch been attempted/exhausted' rather than purely on item possession.

Both new transition passages define two choices structurally (so the automated 'single-choice' graph check in src/validation/graph.ts, which only counts raw choice array length, does not fire), but because closet-report-to-gathering/closet-report-to-wall carry exactly complementary requires (notFlags:[have-logbook-page] vs flags:[have-logbook-page], same for clue-report's pair on have-brass-key), exactly one of the two choices is ever actually selectable at runtime -- the reader always sees one live choice and one permanently grayed-out choice with a lockedHint on every visit to closet-report and clue-report. This mirrors the existing 'gathering' passage's own pattern (2 of its 3 choices are similarly flag-gated) so it is not a new convention, but it means these two 'new' passages do not in practice offer the reader two live options, which is worth the narrative-designer's awareness if the intent was genuine branching rather than a disguised one-way corridor.
